title: Protein Prep Book
blurb: Sixteen batch-cook recipes built for a lean-muscle goal. Cook on Sunday, eat well all week.

recipes.time: Prep 15 min + 20 min marinate · Cook 35 min
recipes.eq: Large deep skillet or Dutch oven, pot or rice cooker
i: 900 g chicken breast, cut into 1-inch cubes
1 tsp salt, divided, plus more to taste
1 cup dry basmati rice + 1½ cups water
s: Marinate|In a bowl, mix the Greek yogurt, 1 tbsp garam masala and ½ tsp salt. Add the chicken cubes and stir until every piece is coated. Cover and refrigerate at least 20 minutes (up to overnight for more flavour).

Start the rice|Rinse the basmati in a sieve under cold water until the water runs mostly clear (about 30 seconds). Add rice and 1½ cups water to a pot with a pinch of salt, bring to a boil, then cover, drop to the lowest heat and cook 12 minutes. Turn off the heat and leave it covered 10 minutes, then fluff with a fork. (Or use a rice cooker.)

Sear the chicken|Heat the oil in your large skillet over medium-high until it shimmers. Shake excess marinade off the chicken and add it in a single layer (do this in 2 batches if it doesn't fit). Leave it untouched 3 minutes so it browns, then flip and cook 2 more minutes. It doesn't need to be cooked through yet. Move to a plate.

Build the sauce base|Lower heat to medium. Add the butter to the same pan (don't clean it; the browned bits are flavour). Once melted, add the onion and a pinch of salt and cook, stirring occasionally, 6–8 minutes until soft and light golden.
Bloom the spices|Add garlic, ginger, the remaining 1 tbsp garam masala and chili powder. Stir constantly for 60 seconds until very fragrant. Don't let the garlic brown.
Simmer|Pour in the passata and ½ tsp salt, stir, and bring to a gentle bubble. Cook 10 minutes, stirring now and then, until it thickens slightly and darkens in colour.

Finish|Stir in the coconut milk, then return the chicken and any juices from the plate. Simmer uncovered 8–10 minutes until the chicken is cooked through (no pink in the centre, 165°F/74°C). Taste and add salt if needed. If the sauce gets too thick, splash in water.
Portion|Divide rice into 4 containers (about ¾ cup cooked each), spoon chicken and sauce alongside, and top with cilantro. Cool 20 minutes uncovered before sealing.
recipes.rh: Microwave covered 2–2½ minutes, stirring halfway. Add a splash of water to the rice.
recipes.x: Freezes well up to 3 months. Freeze sauce and chicken without the rice for best texture.
g: Produce|Cilantro, dill, green onion, parsley, chives

recipes.eq: Large skillet, pot or rice cooker
i: 1 tbsp chipotle in adobo, finely chopped (plus 1 tsp of the sauce)
1 can (540 ml) black beans, drained and rinsed
1 cup dry rice + 2 cups water (or 1½ for basmati)
½ cup 0% Greek yogurt (as sour cream)
s: Start the rice|Rinse the rice, then add it to a pot with the water and a pinch of salt. Boil, cover, reduce to low and cook 15 minutes (12 for basmati). Rest covered 10 minutes off the heat.

Brown the turkey|Heat oil in your large skillet over medium-high. Add the turkey and break it apart with a wooden spoon. Cook 7–9 minutes, stirring every minute or so, until no pink remains and some bits are browned. Turkey is lean, so don't expect much fat; if a little collects, leave it.

Season|Sprinkle in chili powder, cumin, paprika, garlic powder and salt. Add the chipotle and adobo sauce. Stir 1 minute to toast the spices, then pour in the ½ cup water and scrape the bottom of the pan. Simmer 3 minutes until the liquid mostly cooks off and coats the meat.
Add beans and corn|Stir in the black beans and frozen corn. Cook 3–4 minutes until everything is hot. Squeeze in the juice of 1 lime. Taste; add more salt or chipotle if you want more kick.
Make lime rice|Fluff the rice, then stir in the zest and juice of the second lime and the cilantro.

Portion|Divide rice into 4 containers and top with the turkey mixture. Put salsa and yogurt in small side containers (or a corner of the container). Pack the shredded romaine separately so it stays crisp; add it after reheating.
recipes.rh: Microwave rice and turkey 2 minutes. Top with cold salsa, yogurt and romaine after heating.
recipes.x: Swap in extra-lean ground beef any week; drain any fat after browning.
g: Produce|Cilantro, dill, green onion, parsley, chives

recipes.eq: Sheet pan, cast iron or heavy skillet, sturdy flat spatula
i: ½ tsp garlic powder, salt and pepper
1 tsp salt + ½ tsp pepper for the beef
Sauce: ½ cup 0% Greek yogurt, 2 tbsp light mayo, 1 tbsp ketchup, 1 tsp yellow mustard, 2 tbsp pickle relish, ¼ tsp paprika, pinch garlic powder
s: Roast the potatoes|Heat oven to 425°F (220°C). On a sheet pan, toss potato halves with olive oil, garlic powder, salt and pepper. Turn them cut side down. Roast 25–30 minutes until the undersides are deep golden and a fork slides in easily. No need to flip.
Make the sauce|While potatoes roast, stir all sauce ingredients together in a small bowl. Taste; add more relish for tang or ketchup for sweetness. Refrigerate.
Portion the beef|Divide the beef into 8 loose balls (about 110 g each). Don't pack them tight; loose meat smashes thinner and browns better.
Heat the pan hard|Put your cast iron over high heat for 3–4 minutes with no oil, until it's smoking lightly. Open a window or turn on the fan.

Smash|Place 2–3 balls in the pan with space between. Immediately press each one flat with your spatula as hard as you can (a piece of parchment between the spatula and meat stops sticking) to about ¼ inch thick. Season the tops with salt and pepper.

Flip and melt|Cook 2 minutes without moving until the edges are dark brown and crisp. Scrape under each patty firmly with the spatula to keep the crust, flip, and lay half a cheese slice on each. Cook 1 more minute. Repeat with the rest, wiping out the pan between batches if it gets too smoky.

Chop and portion|Let patties rest 2 minutes, then roughly chop them. Divide potatoes and beef between 4 containers. Pack romaine, tomato, onion and pickles in a separate container or a lidded side section, and sauce in small cups.
recipes.rh: Microwave potatoes and beef 1½–2 minutes (or air fry 4 minutes at 375°F to re-crisp). Add cold salad and sauce after.
recipes.x: Sauce keeps 5 days; make a double batch.
g: Pantry & sauces|Light mayo, ketchup, mustard, relish

recipes.t: Sticky, sweet, the one you'll repeat.
recipes.eq: Sheet pan, large skillet, pot or rice cooker
i: 900 g chicken breast, cut into 1-inch cubes
½ tsp salt, ¼ tsp pepper
Sesame seeds and sliced green onion, to finish
s: Prep|Heat oven to 425°F (220°C). Start the rice (rinse, boil in 2 cups water, cover on low 15 minutes, rest 10). In a small bowl, whisk honey, soy, garlic and rice vinegar; set aside. In a cup, stir cornstarch into cold water for the slurry.
Roast the broccoli|Toss florets with 1 tsp oil and a pinch of salt on a sheet pan. Roast 15–18 minutes until the edges are browned and crispy.
Coat the chicken|Pat chicken dry with paper towel. Toss with salt, pepper and 1 tbsp cornstarch. This thin coating is what makes the sauce cling and turn sticky.

Sear|Heat oil in your large skillet over medium-high until shimmering. Add chicken in a single layer (2 batches if needed). Cook 3 minutes without touching, flip, and cook 3–4 more until golden and cooked through (165°F/74°C, no pink inside).
Sauce|Return all chicken to the pan and drop heat to medium. Pour in the honey-soy mixture; it will bubble fast. Stir 1–2 minutes.
Thicken|Stir the slurry again (it settles), pour it in and stir constantly 30–60 seconds until the sauce turns glossy and coats the chicken. Take it off the heat immediately; honey burns quickly.
Portion|Divide rice, broccoli and chicken into 4 containers and spoon all the pan sauce over. Scatter sesame seeds and green onion.
recipes.rh: Microwave covered 2 minutes. The sauce loosens as it warms.
recipes.x: Cook an extra 600 g of plain seasoned chicken in the same session for the Caesar wraps.
g: Produce|Cilantro, dill, green onion, parsley, chives

recipes.eq: Sheet pan, large skillet, small saucepan, pot or rice cooker
i: 800 g chicken breast, cut into 1-inch cubes
1 tsp garlic powder, 1 tsp paprika, ½ tsp salt, ¼ tsp pepper
Cheese sauce: 1 can (370 ml) 2% evaporated milk, 1 tbsp cornstarch, 120 g light old cheddar (shredded), ½ tsp Dijon mustard, ¼ tsp garlic powder, pinch cayenne, salt to taste
s: Start the rice and oven|Heat oven to 425°F (220°C). Rinse rice and cook in 2 cups water (boil, cover, lowest heat 15 minutes, rest 10).
Roast the broccoli|Toss florets with 1 tsp oil and a pinch of salt on a sheet pan. Roast 15–18 minutes until tender with crispy browned edges.

Cook the chicken|Toss chicken with garlic powder, paprika, salt and pepper. Heat oil in your skillet over medium-high until shimmering. Add chicken in one layer (2 batches if needed), cook 3 minutes untouched, flip, and cook 3–4 more minutes until golden and 165°F/74°C inside.

Heat the milk|For the sauce, pour all but 3 tbsp of the evaporated milk into a small saucepan over medium heat. Heat until steaming with small bubbles at the edge, about 3–4 minutes. Don't let it boil hard.
Thicken|Stir the cornstarch into the reserved 3 tbsp cold evaporated milk until smooth. Whisk it into the hot milk and keep whisking 1–2 minutes until it thickens enough to coat a spoon.

Melt in the cheese|Take the pan off the heat. Add the cheddar a handful at a time, whisking until each addition melts before adding more. Stir in Dijon, garlic powder, cayenne and salt. Off-heat melting keeps it smooth instead of grainy.
Portion|Divide rice, broccoli and chicken into 4 containers. Pour the cheese sauce over the broccoli and chicken, or pack it in small cups if you like it saucier after reheating.
recipes.rh: Microwave covered 2 minutes, stirring halfway. If the sauce has set, stir in 1 tbsp milk.
recipes.x: Evaporated milk is the trick: it gives a cream-sauce texture for a fraction of the fat. Sauce keeps 4 days.

i: 1 tsp Italian seasoning, ½ tsp salt, ¼ tsp pepper
340 g chickpea or lentil pasta (penne or rotini)
s: Even out the chicken|If breasts are thick on one end, place them between plastic wrap and pound with a pan or rolling pin to an even ¾ inch. They'll cook evenly and stay juicy. Season both sides with Italian seasoning, salt and pepper.

Cook the chicken|Heat olive oil in your skillet over medium-high. Lay the chicken in and don't move it for 5–6 minutes until deep golden. Flip, turn heat to medium, and cook 5–6 more minutes until the thickest part reads 165°F/74°C or the juices run clear when cut. Rest on a board 5 minutes, then slice.

Boil the pasta|Bring a large pot of well-salted water to a rolling boil. Cook the pasta 1 minute less than the package says; legume pasta goes mushy fast. Before draining, scoop out ½ cup of the pasta water.
Wilt the veg|Drain the pasta and return it to the hot pot off the heat. Add spinach and tomatoes and stir; the heat will wilt the spinach in about a minute.
Sauce it|Add the pesto and 3–4 tbsp of the reserved pasta water. Stir well until the pesto coats everything in a loose sauce (add more water if it looks dry, since it tightens in the fridge).
Finish and portion|Fold in the sliced chicken and parmesan. Divide into 4 containers.
recipes.rh: Add 1 tbsp water, microwave covered 1½–2 minutes, stir. Also good cold like pasta salad.

recipes.time: Prep 20 min + 20 min marinate · Cook 25 min
recipes.eq: Sheet pan or skillet, box grater, pot
i: Marinade: juice of 1 lemon, 1 tbsp olive oil, 1 tbsp minced garlic, 2 tsp dried oregano, 1 tsp paprika, 1 tsp salt, ½ tsp pepper
Tzatziki: 1 cup 0% Greek yogurt, ½ cucumber grated, 1 tsp minced garlic, 1 tbsp fresh dill (or 1 tsp dried), 1 tsp lemon juice, pinch of salt
Salad: 1 cucumber, 2 tomatoes, ½ red onion, all diced, + squeeze of lemon and pinch of salt
s: Marinate|Whisk marinade ingredients in a bowl or zip bag, add the chicken thighs, and massage to coat. Refrigerate at least 20 minutes (up to 24 hours).
Start the rice or orzo|Rice: rinse and cook as usual (2 cups water, 15 min on low, rest 10). Orzo: boil in salted water 8–9 minutes, drain, and toss with a few drops of olive oil so it doesn't clump.

Cook the chicken|Heat oven to 425°F (220°C). Lay thighs flat on a lined sheet pan with space between them. Roast 18–22 minutes until the edges char slightly and the thickest piece reads 175°F/80°C (thighs taste better cooked a bit past 165°F). For more colour, broil the last 2 minutes. Or pan-fry over medium-high, 5–6 minutes per side.

Make the tzatziki|Grate the half cucumber on the large holes of a box grater. Pile it in a clean towel and squeeze hard over the sink until no more water comes out; this stops the sauce going runny. Mix with yogurt, garlic, dill, lemon juice and salt.
Make the salad|Toss diced cucumber, tomato and red onion with lemon and salt. Keep it separate from hot food.
Slice|Rest the chicken 5 minutes, then slice into strips.
Portion|Divide rice, chicken and feta into 4 containers. Pack salad and tzatziki separately so the rice doesn't get soggy.
recipes.rh: Microwave rice and chicken 2 minutes. Add cold salad and tzatziki after.
g: Produce|Cilantro, dill, green onion, parsley, chives

recipes.eq: Lined sheet pan, small saucepan, pot
i: 4 salmon fillets, about 150 g each, skin on or off
Teriyaki: ¼ cup low-sodium soy sauce, 2 tbsp honey, 1 tbsp rice vinegar, 1 tsp minced garlic, 1 tsp grated ginger, 2 tbsp water, 1 tsp cornstarch
s: Make the teriyaki|In a small saucepan, whisk soy, honey, vinegar, garlic, ginger, water and cornstarch. Bring to a simmer over medium, stirring, and cook 1–2 minutes until it thickens enough to coat a spoon. Pour half into a separate bowl for brushing (so raw-fish brush never touches the serving sauce).
Start the rice|Rinse and cook rice (2 cups water, boil, cover on low 15 minutes, rest 10).
Prep the salmon|Heat oven to 400°F (200°C). Pat fillets dry, place on a lined sheet pan skin side down, and season lightly with salt. Brush generously with the brushing half of the sauce.

Bake|Bake 12–14 minutes, until the salmon flakes easily at the thickest point and reads 130–140°F (54–60°C). It will keep cooking a little on the tray. For a glazed top, brush once more and broil 1–2 minutes, watching closely.
Cook the edamame|Boil or microwave edamame 3–4 minutes until hot, drain, and salt lightly.
Portion|Divide rice into 4 containers. Add a fillet, edamame, cucumber and carrot to each. Drizzle the reserved teriyaki over the salmon and finish with sesame seeds and green onion.
recipes.rh: Microwave at 50% power for 2–2½ minutes to avoid drying out the salmon, or eat it cold over warm rice.
recipes.x: Eat within 2–3 days, so plan it early in the week.
g: Produce|Cilantro, dill, green onion, parsley, chives

recipes.t: Egg-dipped cod, lemon butter and wine sauce.
recipes.eq: Sheet pan, large non-stick skillet, 3 shallow dishes
i: 900 g cod fillets, cut into 4 portions
½ tsp salt, ¼ tsp pepper
Egg dip: 2 eggs, ¼ cup liquid egg whites, 2 tbsp grated parmesan, 1 tbsp chopped parsley
1 tbsp butter + 1 tbsp oil for frying
Sauce: 1 tbsp butter, 1 tsp minced garlic, ½ cup dry white wine (or extra broth), ½ cup chicken broth, juice of 1 lemon, 1 tbsp cold butter, 1 tbsp capers (optional), parsley
800 g baby potatoes, halved + 1 tsp oil
s: Roast the potatoes|Heat oven to 425°F (220°C). Toss potatoes with oil, salt and pepper, turn cut side down on a sheet pan, and roast 25–30 minutes. Add the green beans to the same pan for the last 12 minutes.
Set up the station|Put flour in one shallow dish. Whisk eggs, egg whites, parmesan and parsley in a second. Leave a clean plate at the end.
Dry and season the fish|Pat the cod very dry with paper towel; wet fish makes the coating slide off. Season both sides with salt and pepper.
Dredge and dip|Coat each piece lightly in flour and tap off the excess, then dip in the egg mixture so it's fully covered, letting extra drip back into the dish.

Pan-fry|Heat butter and oil in the skillet over medium until the butter foams. Lay the cod in (don't crowd it) and cook 3–4 minutes until the underside is golden. Flip gently with a fish spatula and cook 3–4 more minutes until the thickest part flakes easily and is opaque all the way through (145°F/63°C). Move to a plate.

Build the sauce|Wipe out any burnt bits but leave the golden ones. Over medium, melt 1 tbsp butter and add garlic for 30 seconds. Pour in the wine and let it bubble 2 minutes until reduced by half. Add broth and lemon juice and simmer 3 minutes.
Finish the sauce|Take the pan off the heat and swirl in the cold butter until the sauce turns slightly glossy. Stir in capers and parsley. Taste for salt.
Portion|Divide potatoes, green beans and cod into 4 containers. Pack the sauce in small cups so the coating stays intact; pour it over after reheating.
recipes.rh: Best: oven or air fryer at 350°F for 6–8 minutes. Otherwise microwave at 50% power for 1½–2 minutes. Warm the sauce separately and pour over.
recipes.x: Eat within 2 days. Sole or haddock work the same way.
g: Produce|Cilantro, dill, green onion, parsley, chives

recipes.t: Silky cream sauce, fruity peppery bite.
recipes.eq: Sheet pan, large skillet, pot or rice cooker, mortar or zip bag
i: 900 g haddock (or halibut or cod), cut into 4 portions
½ tsp salt, ¼ tsp black pepper
1 bunch asparagus, woody ends snapped off + 1 tsp oil
Sauce: 1 tbsp butter, 1 shallot finely diced, 1 tbsp pink peppercorns, ⅓ cup dry white wine (or broth), ⅔ cup 2% evaporated milk, 1 tsp Dijon, squeeze of lemon, chopped chives
s: Rice and asparagus|Cook rice (rinse, 1½ cups water, boil, cover on low 15 minutes, rest 10). Heat oven to 425°F, toss asparagus with oil and salt, and roast 10–12 minutes until just tender.
Crush the peppercorns|Put pink peppercorns in a zip bag and press with the bottom of a pan, or use a mortar. You want them cracked, not powdered.

Sear the fish|Pat the haddock very dry and season. Heat oil in the skillet over medium-high until shimmering. Lay fish in and cook 3 minutes without moving until golden underneath. Flip carefully and cook 2–3 minutes more until opaque and flaking at the thickest part. Move to a plate.
Start the sauce|Lower heat to medium. Add butter and shallot and cook 2–3 minutes until soft. Add most of the pink peppercorns (save a pinch for garnish) and stir 30 seconds.
Reduce|Pour in the wine and let it bubble 2 minutes until reduced by about half.

Make it creamy|Lower to medium-low. Stir in evaporated milk and Dijon and simmer gently 3–4 minutes until it thickens enough to coat a spoon. Keep it at a gentle bubble; a hard boil can split it. Add lemon, salt to taste and chives.
Portion|Divide rice, asparagus and fish into 4 containers. Spoon sauce over the fish and finish with the reserved peppercorns.
recipes.rh: Microwave at 50% power for 2–2½ minutes to keep the fish tender.
recipes.x: Eat within 2 days. Pink peppercorns are related to cashews, so skip them if anyone eating has a cashew allergy.
g: Produce|Cilantro, dill, green onion, parsley, chives

recipes.time: Prep 15 min + 30 min soak · Cook 35 min
recipes.eq: Air fryer or sheet pan, cast iron skillet, meat thermometer
i: 900 g top sirloin, 2–4 steaks about 1 inch thick
1 tsp salt, 1 tsp coarse black pepper
1 tbsp butter, 2 garlic cloves (smashed), 2 sprigs thyme
800 g russet potatoes + 1 tbsp oil, ½ tsp salt
Light béarnaise: ½ cup 0% Greek yogurt, 1 tbsp melted butter, 1 tsp Dijon, 1 tsp dried tarragon, 1 small shallot finely minced, 1 tsp lemon juice, salt
s: Cut and soak the fries|Cut potatoes (skin on is fine) into ⅓-inch sticks. Soak in cold water 30 minutes. This pulls out surface starch so they crisp instead of going limp.
Temper the steak|While fries soak, take the steak out of the fridge, pat it very dry, and season heavily on both sides with salt and pepper. Leave it on the counter.

Cook the fries|Drain the fries and dry them thoroughly with a towel (water is the enemy of crisp). Toss with oil and salt. Air fryer: 380°F for 18–22 minutes, shaking every 6 minutes. Oven: spread in one layer on parchment at 450°F for 30–35 minutes, flipping halfway.
Make the béarnaise|Stir yogurt, melted butter, Dijon, tarragon, shallot, lemon and salt together. Let it sit 10 minutes so the tarragon softens.

Sear the steak|Heat cast iron over high until it just starts to smoke. Add the oil, then the steaks. Don't touch them for 3 minutes. Flip and cook 2–3 minutes more. For prep, aim for 125°F (rare) inside; it cooks further when reheated and ends up medium-rare.
Baste|Turn heat to medium, add butter, garlic and thyme. Tilt the pan and spoon the foaming butter over the steaks for 45 seconds.
Rest and slice|Rest steaks on a board 10 minutes, then slice across the grain into strips.
Portion|Divide steak and fries between 4 containers. Pack arugula and béarnaise separately.
recipes.rh: Fries: air fry at 375°F for 4–5 minutes to re-crisp. Steak: microwave at 50% for 30–45 seconds, or eat it cold sliced. Add arugula and béarnaise after.
recipes.x: Keeps 3 days. Flank or striploin also work.

recipes.eq: Oven-safe skillet, pot, potato masher, meat thermometer
i: 1 tsp salt, ½ tsp pepper, 1 tsp dried thyme
Mash: 800 g Yukon Gold potatoes, ⅓ cup 0% Greek yogurt, ¼ cup milk, 1 tbsp butter, salt and pepper
Sauce: 1 tsp butter, 1 shallot finely diced, 1 tsp minced garlic, ½ cup chicken broth, ⅔ cup 2% evaporated milk, 1 tbsp Dijon, 1 tbsp grainy mustard, ½ tsp thyme, pepper
s: Trim the pork|Heat oven to 400°F (200°C). Look for the thin shiny membrane (silverskin) on the tenderloin. Slide a knife just under it and cut it away, angling the blade up; it turns chewy if left on. Season all over with salt, pepper and thyme.
Start the mash|Peel and cube potatoes into 1½-inch pieces. Put in a pot, cover with cold water, add 1 tsp salt, and bring to a boil. Simmer 15 minutes until a fork slides through with no resistance.
Sear the pork|Heat oil in the oven-safe skillet over medium-high. Sear the tenderloins on all sides, about 2 minutes per side, 6–8 minutes total, until browned.

Roast|Move the skillet to the oven and roast 12–15 minutes until the centre reads 145°F/63°C. A little pink inside is correct and safe. Move pork to a board and rest 10 minutes. Carefully leave the hot skillet handle covered with a towel.
Finish the mash|Drain the potatoes well and let them steam dry 1 minute in the pot. Mash with butter, then stir in yogurt and milk until creamy. Season with salt and pepper.
Cook the green beans|Steam or microwave the beans with 2 tbsp water, covered, 4 minutes until bright green and tender-crisp. Salt lightly.

Make the sauce|Put the skillet back on the stove over medium (handle is still hot). Add butter and shallot for 2 minutes, then garlic for 30 seconds. Pour in broth and scrape up the browned bits; simmer 3 minutes until reduced by half. Stir in evaporated milk, both mustards and thyme. Simmer gently 3–4 minutes until it coats a spoon. Add pepper and pour in any juices from the resting pork.
Slice and portion|Slice the pork into ½-inch medallions. Divide mash, beans and pork into 4 containers and spoon sauce over the pork so it stays moist.
recipes.rh: Microwave covered 2 minutes, with the sauce over the pork. Add a splash of milk to the mash if it's stiff.
recipes.x: Keeps 4 days. Mash freezes fine; the sauce is best fresh.

recipes.eq: Large bowl, whisk, 4 jars or containers
i: Pinch of salt, ½ tsp cinnamon (optional)
s: Dissolve the protein first|Pour milk into a large bowl, add the protein powder, and whisk hard for 30 seconds until completely smooth. Doing this first prevents dry clumps later.
Mix the base|Whisk in the Greek yogurt, then stir in oats, chia, salt and cinnamon until evenly combined. It should look loose and soupy; the oats and chia absorb a lot of liquid overnight.
Jar it|Divide evenly between 4 jars. Top each with ½ cup frozen berries. Frozen is fine; they thaw overnight and bleed flavour into the oats.
Chill|Seal and refrigerate at least 6 hours or overnight.
Adjust in the morning|If it's too thick, stir in a splash of milk. Eat cold, or microwave 60–90 seconds if you prefer it warm.
recipes.x: Keeps 4 days. Swap chocolate protein and add a tbsp of peanut butter for variety.

recipes.time: Prep 20 min · Cook 20 min · Cool 20 min
recipes.eq: Large non-stick skillet, foil, freezer bag
i: ½ tsp salt, ¼ tsp pepper
s: Cook the filling|Brown the sausage in the skillet over medium-high, breaking it into small crumbles, 6–7 minutes. Add peppers and onion and cook 5 more minutes until soft and any liquid has cooked off. Wet filling makes soggy burritos, so get it dry. Tip into a bowl.

Scramble the eggs|Whisk eggs, egg whites, salt and pepper. Wipe the pan, spray it, and set to medium-low. Pour in eggs and let sit 30 seconds, then slowly push them from the edges to the centre with a spatula. Stop while they still look slightly wet (about 4–5 minutes); they finish cooking when reheated.
Cool the fillings|Spread eggs on a plate and let both fillings cool 10 minutes. Hot filling steams inside the wrap and causes ice crystals and sogginess.
Warm the tortillas|Microwave the stack of tortillas under a damp paper towel for 30 seconds so they fold without cracking.

Assemble|Lay a tortilla flat. In the lower third, add ⅛ of the eggs, ⅛ of the sausage mix, 2 tbsp cheese and 1 tbsp salsa. Fold the bottom edge up over the filling, fold in both sides, then roll up tightly away from you.
Wrap and freeze|Wrap each burrito tightly in foil (or plastic wrap), label with the date, and put them all in a large freezer bag. Freeze flat.
recipes.rh: From frozen: remove foil, wrap in a damp paper towel, microwave 1 minute, flip, 1–1½ more minutes until hot in the centre. For a crisp outside, finish 2 minutes in a dry pan or air fryer.

recipes.time: Prep 15 min · Cook 10 min (with pre-cooked chicken)
i: 600 g cooked chicken breast, sliced or chopped (from your honey garlic prep day, cooked plain)
s: Cook the chicken if you haven't|Season 600 g raw chicken breast with salt, pepper and garlic powder. Pan-cook over medium-high 5–6 minutes per side to 165°F/74°C. Rest 5 minutes and slice thinly.
Crisp the bacon|Cook turkey bacon in a dry skillet over medium, 3–4 minutes per side, until crisp. Cool on paper towel, then crumble.
Mix the dressing|Stir Caesar dressing, Greek yogurt, lemon juice and lots of pepper together. The yogurt adds protein and cuts calories without losing the flavour.
Dry the romaine|Make sure the chopped romaine is completely dry (use a salad spinner or towel). Wet lettuce makes wraps soggy by day 2.
Toss|In a large bowl, toss romaine, chicken, bacon and parmesan with the dressing until everything is lightly coated.

Roll|Warm tortillas 20 seconds in the microwave. Pile a quarter of the filling in the lower third of each, fold up the bottom, fold in the sides, and roll tightly. Wrap each in foil and cut in half at serving time.
recipes.x: For longer storage, keep the dressing separate and toss it in the morning.

recipes.t: Tastes like dessert, eats like a shake.
i: Berries or a few chocolate chips to top (optional)
s: Combine the dry|In a bowl, mix protein powder, cocoa and salt so the cocoa doesn't clump.
Whisk in the yogurt|Add the yogurt and whisk hard for about a minute. It will look stiff and streaky at first, then turn smooth and dark.
Adjust the texture|Add milk 1 tbsp at a time, whisking between, until it's thick and spoonable like pudding. Different protein powders absorb different amounts, so go by feel.
Portion and chill|Divide between 4 containers and refrigerate at least 1 hour. It thickens as it sits. Top right before eating.

Produce: Cilantro, dill, green onion, parsley, chives

plan: Two bowls for lunch and dinner, plus one breakfast. Rotate next week so you don't burn out.
2 cups dry rice covers two bowl recipes. Rice cooker or pot, then forget it.
Anything roasting (potatoes, broccoli) goes in now on sheet pans.
Chicken sits in its marinade for the 15–20 minutes you spend on everything else.
One big pan, one recipe after another. Don't wash it between batches unless flavours clash.
Tzatziki, burger sauce and stir-fry sauces are all no-cook stirs.
Let food cool 20 minutes, split into containers, write the day on the lid.
Eat Thursday onward from the freezer. Salmon: eat within 2–3 days, don't freeze after cooking.

sample.note: On heavy training days, add a breakfast burrito or an extra scoop of rice to push calories up; building muscle needs enough fuel, not just protein.

containers: Ten glass 3-cup containers, four jars for oats, and a roll of freezer bags for burritos. Glass reheats better and doesn't hold sauce stains.
fine: Macros are estimates per serving based on standard grocery products. Check brands in your tracking app if you're counting closely.

snacks.note: A 50 g bag. Check sugar; teriyaki styles are the worst offenders.
Two sticks. Keeps in a bag or the car forever.
Sea salt or BBQ. Crunchy, the closest thing to chips with fibre.
A small handful, about 30 g. Buy the portion packs if the big bag disappears.
Quest or Legendary. Scratches the crisps itch for real protein.
A tub with everything-bagel seasoning and crackers. Cheap protein.
Two rounds. Fridge staple that survives a backpack.
100 g of deli meat rolled with cheese. Assembles in a minute.
Microwave 3 minutes and salt heavily. Filling for very few calories.
Flavoured pouches need no draining, no fork, no smell in the sink.
Buy them pre-cooked or boil a dozen on prep day. Two eggs a serving.
